title: Zack and Miri Make a Porno
full_review:
Romantic aspirations are undercut, in writer-director Kevin Smith's wayward comedy "Zack and Miri Make a Porno" (Weinstein) by a frivolous approach to human sexuality.

With their water and electricity cut, cash-strapped roommates and long-standing friends Zack (Seth Rogen) and Miri (Elizabeth Banks) strike on the idea of paying their bills by making a pornographic film together. Having gained the financial backing of Zack's co-worker Delaney (Craig Robinson), they easily assemble a cast of congenial amateurs (Traci Lords and Jason Mewes among others).

Yet, as the shooting of their own scene approaches, both fear the effects on their stable, platonic relationship.

Instead of a profit-driven assault on human dignity, pornography is portrayed here as, at worst, a lark and, at best, a means of self-fulfillment.

The film contains strong sexual content, including graphic nonmarital and aberrant sexual activity, adultery, frontal male and female, upper female and rear nudity, much sexual and some scatological humor, pervasive rough and crude language and a few uses of profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. Motion Picture Association of America rating, R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
